title: Kinley Rasmus makes more LLWS history. Here’s when she can pitch next
content:
Another day, another history-making moment for 12-year-old Kinley Rasmus at the Little League World Series.

One day after tying Mo’ne Davis’ record for most strikeouts in a tournament (14) by a female pitcher, Rasmus set the record for the most hits in a single tournament (five) by a female player. Her efforts on offense helped Phenix City, Ala., escape elimination in a 4-2 win over Tacoma, Wash., and live to fight another day in the U.S. bracket of this year’s tournament.

In turn, it’s opened the door for a potential third appearance for the daughter of former big leaguer Cory Rasmus, one that could have a championship and history on the line.

For Phenix City to reach that point, they’ll need to take care of business Wednesday against Hamilton, Ohio. Because Rasmus appeared in Monday’s game, one in which she came on in relief to fire 4 2/3 scoreless innings with six strikeouts (54 total pitches), Rasmus must have a mandated three days of rest.

That Rasmus managed to stay under the 66-pitch threshold even as Monday’s contest extended into extras has provided a particularly interesting lane for Rasmus’ future usage.

Should Phenix City continue to win, the next time Rasmus could be used is Saturday, Aug. 29, in the U.S. championship game. The winner of that game and the winner of the international bracket will meet Sunday for the finale.

In that instance, Phenix City will have to decide if Rasmus is worth deploying in the U.S. championship game, the finale (if they win) or a third-place consolation game (if they lose the U.S. championship).

There is a middle ground where Rasmus can appear in both, so long as she throws under 20 pitches.

In any situation, her next strikeout, whichever day she pitches next, will be history-making.
